_comment: WC2026 ROUND OF 16 (bracket tie 91: winner of Portugal-Croatia vs winner of Spain-Austria) -- the IBERIAN DERBY. KNOCKOUT: no draw -- level after 90' -> extra time -> penalties, so the deliverable is who ADVANCES. Winner meets the USA-Belgium winner in the quarter-finals. Nominal bracket orientation is Portugal (home, feeder 77) vs Spain (away, feeder 78) on a neutral venue; modelled here with SPAIN as home (the slight favourite) for clarity -- immaterial on a neutral venue. Routes: Spain WON Group H with ZERO conceded (0-0 Cape Verde, 4-0 Saudi Arabia, 1-0 Uruguay; 7 pts, GF 5 GA 0, rating 94) -- AIRTIGHT defence -- then ROUTED Austria 3-0 in the R32 (another clean sheet). Spain has conceded essentially nothing all tournament; devastating when the game opens (4-0, 3-0) but can be BLUNT vs a good defensive side (0-0 Cape Verde). Portugal finished 2nd in Group K (1-1 DR Congo, 4-0 Uzbekistan, 0-0 Colombia; 5 pts, GF 5 GA 1, rating 90) -- solid defence (GA 1), can be frustrated by / can frustrate a block (0-0 Colombia) -- then edged Croatia 2-1 in the R32. Class gap is SMALL (~4, 94 vs 90) -> Spain a SLIGHT favourite by class + form (a 3-0 rout vs Portugal's 2-1 grind). KEY texture: two ELITE sides with STRONG defences -> a TIGHT, tense, LOW-to-moderate-scoring derby (1-1/1-0/0-0 shape), NOT a shootout; near a coin-flip with Spain edging it; HIGH extra-time/penalty risk. BTTS: this is the rule's EXCEPTION for BTTS-Yes -- a near-even tie between two attacking sides -- BUT both also defend elite (Spain airtight, Portugal solid), so BTTS is kept NEAR-NEUTRAL (~51%), not forced either way: both can score, both can keep a clean sheet (Spain CS 34% -- can shut Portugal out; Portugal CS 24% -- can frustrate Spain like Cape Verde did). Low total (2.50), Under lean. Home = Spain (nominal; neutral venue). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

_postmatch.verdict: Clean process hit -- side, texture AND margin all right. Spain advanced as the slight favourite (59.2%), won 1-0 (a top-2 scoreline at 10.6%), kept a clean sheet (the 34% branch), and it was Under 2.5 (55%) / BTTS-No -- exactly the TIGHT, low-scoring derby I described (two elite defences, low total 2.50, 1-1/1-0/0-0 cluster). The near-neutral BTTS (51%) tipped to No as the low-scoring texture implied, and Spain's airtight defence delivered the clean sheet that edged it. Notably, this is the RIGHT-SIDE of the same-day Mexico-England lesson: there I predicted low and it went 3-2 because Mexico's group defence was FLATTERED by weak opposition; HERE the low read WORKED because Spain's and Portugal's defences are GENUINELY elite (Spain 0 conceded vs real sides incl. Uruguay; Portugal held Colombia) -- so the 'two good defences -> low total' read holds when the defences are real, and fails when they are group-flattered. Spain's slight class + form edge (a 3-0 rout in the R32 vs Portugal's 2-1 grind) showed as the single decisive goal.
_postmatch.lesson: The 'two good defences -> tight, low-scoring, Under, clean-sheet-decides' read is CORRECT when both defences are genuinely elite against quality (Spain/Portugal), and WRONG when a defensive record is flattered by weak group opposition (Mexico). Same-day A/B test: Spain-Portugal 1-0 (real defences, low read landed) vs Mexico-England 3-2 (flattered defence, low read failed). Calibrate the total on the quality of BOTH the attacks AND the defences vs the level they earned it at. And in a near-coin-flip derby, the slight favourite with the marginally better form/defence edges it by the odd goal -- advancement 59% -> a 1-0. Keep the near-neutral BTTS honest (don't force it) but let a genuinely elite defence pull the clean-sheet/Under branch up.
